goal: Identify the strongest defensible custom role for the candidate inside TypeSafe, grounded in current TypeSafe needs and exact repository evidence, then produce a public-safe role charter and application narrative that make the contribution concrete without inflating workflow, governance, formal-methods, or autonomy claims.
context: The candidate founded CyberAlchemy and describes a practice spanning governed human-AI workflows, typed domain specifications, research, system design, cybernetics, domain modeling, category theory, and Lean. TypeSafe publicly seeks reliable and general AI systems for economically valuable automation and explicitly invites candidates to create their own role, but the repository does not itself establish frontier-model training, production-ML, GPU-kernel, or synthetic-data ownership. Research the whole repository with deliberate focus on cyberAlchemy-v2/, projects/domainspec-v2/, and arcanum/, re-open TypeSafe's live pages, and treat a 'perfect role' as a falsifiable role hypothesis rather than a promised conclusion. This is private research only: do not edit product or authority files, publish private prose, contact TypeSafe, or submit an application.
anti_bias_global: Evidence-to-employer-value tension across authority and reliability theory, typed specification and delivered traceability, operational autonomy and current lab needs, followed by independent attacks on ownership, non-vacuity, and title or claim collapse.

groups.anti_bias: Composite methodology and source-corpus axis: formal authority mapping in CyberAlchemy v2, empirical traceability and receipt audit in DomainSpec v2, and adversarial operational-plus-market fit across Arcanum, the whole repository, and live TypeSafe sources.

predicted_disagreements.statement: Agent 0 runs formal authority and reliability mapping over the CyberAlchemy v2 corpus while agent 1 runs empirical traceability and receipt audit over the DomainSpec v2 corpus on the composite methodology and source-corpus axis; a bias in agent 0 toward elegant governance abstractions would be exposed by agent 1's demand for closed execution evidence, while a bias in agent 1 toward local artifact completion would be exposed by agent 0's demand for explicit judgment, authority, and failure boundaries.

Agent 0 runs private authority-model analysis while agent 2 runs adversarial operational and current-employer-fit analysis across public Arcanum, repository-wide receipts, and live TypeSafe sources on the composite methodology and source-corpus axis; a bias in agent 0 toward internally coherent but employer-opaque language would be exposed by agent 2, while a bias in agent 2 toward marketable phrasing would be exposed by agent 0 if it erases proof ceilings or human authority.

Agent 1 runs artifact-level DomainSpec v2 traceability analysis while agent 2 runs operational lifecycle and live TypeSafe role-fit analysis on the composite methodology and source-corpus axis; a bias in agent 1 toward specification machinery as the product would be exposed by agent 2's demand for an economically valuable lab outcome, while a bias in agent 2 toward a broad reliability title would be exposed by agent 1's exact evidence and delivery receipts.

groups.anti_bias: Attack-vector axis: existing-role and field precedent, concrete TypeSafe-value non-vacuity, and definitional plus claim-scope collapse.

predicted_disagreements.statement: Agent 0 attacks whether the proposed ownership already belongs to current TypeSafe or established industry roles while agent 1 attacks whether the role can deliver a falsifiable 90-day lab outcome on the attack-vector axis; a bias in agent 0 toward conventional titles would be exposed by agent 1 if no existing role owns the cross-functional value, while a bias in agent 1 toward an attractive pilot would be exposed by agent 0 if the work simply belongs to product, research engineering, or developer advocacy.

Agent 0 runs precedent and ownership attack while agent 2 runs definitional and claim-scope collapse attack on the attack-vector axis; a bias in agent 0 toward renaming an existing profession would be exposed by agent 2's collapse tests, while a bias in agent 2 toward semantic purity would be exposed by agent 0 if a standard intelligible title already carries the needed ownership.

Agent 1 runs non-vacuity attack through concrete TypeSafe outcomes while agent 2 runs definitional and evidence-boundary attack on the attack-vector axis; a bias in agent 1 toward ambitious deliverables would be exposed by agent 2 if they require unproved model-training or production authority, while a bias in agent 2 toward narrow safe wording would be exposed by agent 1 if it leaves no economically valuable responsibility.

agents.angle: Precedent and ownership attack: test the role against TypeSafe's current openings and adjacent research-operations, product, reliability, evals, governance, systems-design, and developer-relations roles.
agents.initial_prompt: Attack only precedent and ownership using the synthesized candidate package and live primary TypeSafe pages. Verify the current open-role set and search current primary job sources for nearby TypeSafe ownership. Identify standard industry role families that already own each proposed responsibility. A found owner is BUILD-FROM-OWNED or ALREADY-DEPLOYED, not a KILL. Require the final title to be intelligible to a frontier lab and the mandate to fill a real gap rather than manufacture uniqueness. Return exact citations, overlap matrix, title repairs, and a PRECEDENT-CLEAN / BUILD-FROM-OWNED / ALREADY-DEPLOYED posture for every candidate. Do not edit files or infer TypeSafe's private roadmap. Target about 2800 tokens.

agents.angle: Non-vacuity attack: require one high-value 90-day witness connecting frontier-model behavior to reliable real-world work without pretending workflow governance changes model weights.
agents.initial_prompt: Attack only non-vacuity. For each candidate role, demand a smallest concrete 30/60/90-day witness TypeSafe could inspect and falsify: input problem, collaborators, artifact or experiment, success/failure criteria, evidence collected, and decision enabled. Reject responsibilities that are only frameworks, diagrams, governance documents, process overhead, evaluation theater, or generic cross-functional glue. Also reject any witness that requires credentials not established by the repository, such as owning distributed training, GPU kernels, novel model architectures, production synthetic-data pipelines, or model-level reliability results. Return GO or KILL per candidate with bounded repairs. Do not edit files. Target about 2800 tokens.

agents.angle: Definitional and claim-boundary attack: test whether the role and every public claim collapse into vague governance, safety branding, product management, systems architecture, or unsupported frontier-model expertise.
agents.initial_prompt: Attack only definitional soundness and claim scope. Test whether the role's nouns correspond to distinct behavior, ownership, artifacts, and decisions. Reject or repair collapse among reliability, safety, governance, evals, specification, product, systems research, research operations, autonomy, accountability, and formal methods. For every public-facing capability claim, require exact repository evidence and downgrade verified/implemented/designed/proposed language correctly. Ensure private DomainSpec, Saturn, and CyberAlchemy v2 prose or paths do not leak into the public charter. Return sound, repair, or KILL per candidate and a list of forbidden phrases. Do not edit files. Target about 2800 tokens.

Only after the parent supplies an exact-binding evidence-closure verdict marked ready, write research/2026-08-01-typesafe-reliable-autonomy-role/findings.md and no other file. The document must lead with one strongest defensible role or a typed KILL. If selected, include: exact title; two conventional search-friendly aliases; one-sentence mandate; TypeSafe problem owned; why now; five to seven responsibilities; interfaces with model research, product, infrastructure, design, and leadership; explicit non-scope; a falsifiable 30/60/90-day plan; success measures; repository evidence matrix with internal claim posture; current TypeSafe fit and overlap map with dated direct links; candid capability and logistics gaps; questions for TypeSafe; a 180-250-word create-your-own-role pitch; a 100-140-word personal introduction; and a public-safe role charter containing no private paths or private authority prose. Explain why 'perfect' cannot be proven and why the selected hypothesis is nevertheless the strongest surviving one. Include a verdict matrix for all candidates. Cite every load-bearing claim. Do not edit research.md, candidate-profile.md, the strategy artifacts, product code, authority files, Arcanum, or Inventory.

Audit findings.md against the frozen sheet, candidate-profile.md, research.md, the exact-binding evidence-closure receipt, and current primary TypeSafe pages. Require: one non-duplicative problem ownership; intelligible title; concrete 30/60/90-day value; exact candidate evidence; honest separation of workflow/system reliability from frontier-model reliability; no invented employment, production, model-training, relocation, visa, or culture-fit claim; public/private safety; useful interfaces; explicit non-scope; candid gaps; and application language that sounds like a builder rather than a governance consultant. Reject a vanity title, generic responsible-AI role, pure process layer, or claims unsupported by repository bytes. Return RECOMMEND_ACCEPT or one bounded writer revision request for the parent final approver. Do not edit files.
